assessmentSummary.identity: One Half-Kneeling Ankle Dorsiflexion Pulse starts with the rear knee and lower leg supported on a pad and the target-side front foot planted through the heel, first metatarsal head, and fifth metatarsal head. Establish a comfortable forward knee-over-middle-toes endpoint without lifting or spinning the target foot. The initial move to that endpoint is setup, not a repetition. Retreat the knee only a small declared distance without returning to the upright half-kneeling start, then re-advance to the same comfortable endpoint. One partial retreat-and-re-advance is one pulse. Front-foot distance, comfortable endpoint, partial-retreat distance, mat thickness, light fingertips on the front thigh without unloading the target foot, visual knee-path target, tempo, breathing prompt, pulse count, sets, rest, and workout context are annotations. A full return to the upright start, standing support, hand-loaded wall support, an isometric hold, resistance band, external load, elevated front foot, active dorsiflexor lift, clinician assistance, calf raise, clinical measurement, or added sport action changes the task.
currentCardFindings: Source 41 is not a direct duplicate of Sources 40, 875, or 1359: rear-knee floor contact changes the support base, balance demand, logistics, duration, comfort constraints, and exact repetition contract.

The current canonical definition and baseline variant are skeletal: anatomy, controlled support contacts, load, fatigue, recovery, environment, population constraints, exact pulse endpoints and count, duration, substitutions, coach support, athlete support, persistence, evidence, calibration, and automated test gates are absent.

The legacy prose says pulse in and out of end range but does not define whether the first advance counts or whether the knee returns to the upright start. The Vortex exact contract treats the first advance as setup and counts one small retreat-and-re-advance while remaining near end range; this candidate definition requires qualified human review.

The legacy age floor, publication state, generic 1 x 10 dose, 20/10/20 scores, and three media IDs lack exact-card calibration, full playback, exactness, captions, accessibility, cue-quality, safety, reviewer, and approval evidence. The kettlebell and active-dorsiflexor video titles indicate adjacent variants and remain quarantined candidates.

currentCardSnapshot.description: Place the rear knee and lower leg on a pad and plant the target-side front foot through the heel, first metatarsal head, and fifth metatarsal head. Advance the front knee over the middle toes to a comfortable endpoint without lifting or spinning the foot; this first advance is setup, not a repetition. Retreat only a small declared distance without returning to the upright half-kneeling start, then re-advance to the same endpoint. Count one partial retreat-and-re-advance as one pulse. Foot placement, comfortable endpoint, retreat distance, pad thickness, light fingertips on the front thigh without unloading the foot, visual target, tempo, breathing, dose, rest, and workout context are annotations. Full return, standing, loaded hand support, a hold, band, weight, elevation, active dorsiflexor lift, clinician force, calf raise, clinical measurement, or added sport action changes the task.

evidence.sourceTitle: Immediate and Short Term Effect of Dry Needling on Triceps Surae Range of Motion and Functional Movement: A Randomized Trial
evidence.sourcePublisher: International Journal of Sports Physical Therapy
claims: The study describes a closed-chain half-kneeling position with the target foot forward, body weight moving forward, and the heel kept down.
It does not define repeated end-range pulses, so Vortex's rear-knee support, partial-retreat endpoint, and count are an explicit candidate contract requiring review.

evidence.sourceTitle: Reliability and validity of a weight-bearing measure of ankle dorsiflexion range of motion
claims: Weight-bearing dorsiflexion uses a planted target foot and forward tibial progression rather than ankle circumduction, calf raising, or impact.
Half-kneeling support and an end-range pulse are controlled task dimensions; they do not classify participant skill or proficiency.

evidence.sourceTitle: How Much Does the Talocrural Joint Contribute to Ankle Dorsiflexion Range of Motion During the Weight-Bearing Lunge Test? A Cross-sectional Radiographic Validity Study
evidence.sourcePublisher: Journal of Orthopaedic & Sports Physical Therapy
claims: Weight-bearing lunge displacement reflects a multisegment task and is not an isolated talocrural measure.
The card tracks foot, ankle, calf, knee, hip, rear-knee support, and trunk stabilization while avoiding single-tissue or diagnostic claims.

evidence.sourceTitle: Immediate and Short Term Effect of Dry Needling on Triceps Surae Range of Motion and Functional Movement: A Randomized Trial
evidence.sourcePublisher: International Journal of Sports Physical Therapy
claims: The published half-kneeling measure advances body weight over the forward foot while the heel remains down.
Vortex adds a fixed foot tripod, middle-toe corridor, comfortable endpoint, small partial retreat, re-advance, and no-upright-return boundary for a countable pulse.

evidence.sourceTitle: Reliability and validity of a weight-bearing measure of ankle dorsiflexion range of motion
claims: Repeatable planted-foot execution requires position and contact control but has low external load and no impact.
The 22/14/22 proposal describes exercise complexity and physical difficulty only, not participant skill, and remains queued for independent calibration.

evidence.sourceTitle: Ankle-Joint Self-Mobilization and CrossFit Training in Patients With Chronic Ankle Instability: A Randomized Controlled Trial
claims: The trial combined multiple ankle self-mobilizations with CrossFit in participants with chronic ankle instability, including a loaded kneeling-lunge exercise.
That protocol cannot establish fatigue or recovery for this unloaded pulse; track actual pulses, range, contact, first fault, symptoms, kneeling time, and overlapping lower-leg work.

evidence.sourceTitle: Sensory-Mapping During the Weight-Bearing Lunge Test Across Chronic Ankle Instability, Copers, and Healthy Controls
claims: Sensation and pain reports during weight-bearing dorsiflexion vary across people and groups.
Selection therefore uses individual front-foot, ankle, calf, knee, rear-knee, kneeling, balance, surface, communication, and cumulative-work checks rather than a demographic or diagnostic threshold.

evidence.sourceTitle: Ankle-Joint Self-Mobilization and CrossFit Training in Patients With Chronic Ankle Instability: A Randomized Controlled Trial
claims: The randomized protocol used three distinct self-mobilization tasks and a clinical population, so its dose is not transferable to an unloaded end-range pulse as a universal prescription.
Vortex's one to three sets of four to ten pulses per side is quarantined delivery guidance and must stop before contacts, endpoints, symptoms, or count degrade.

evidence.sourceTitle: Immediate and Short Term Effect of Dry Needling on Triceps Surae Range of Motion and Functional Movement: A Randomized Trial
evidence.sourcePublisher: International Journal of Sports Physical Therapy
claims: The direct half-kneeling procedure supplies the forward-foot and heel-down setup.
Vortex adds rear-knee padding, tripod contact, initial uncounted endpoint setup, small retreat, same-endpoint re-advance, exact pulse count, side change, and stop and persistence rules.

evidence.sourceTitle: Sensory-Mapping During the Weight-Bearing Lunge Test Across Chronic Ankle Instability, Copers, and Healthy Controls
claims: Pain and sensation location during weight-bearing dorsiflexion are variable and cannot be assigned one universal normal interpretation.

Stop for sharp, increasing, unfamiliar, unstable, neurologic, circulatory, systemic, or rear-knee symptoms; lost contacts; unsafe mat or floor; or a participant request, then follow facility escalation rules.

evidence.sourceTitle: Effect duration of a self-applied talocrural joint mobilization on restricted dorsiflexion: a repeated measures design
claims: A banded self-mobilization changed static weight-bearing lunge dorsiflexion transiently but did not change dynamic forward-step-down dorsiflexion in the study.
This unloaded pulse may be used as preparation when constraints fit, but it cannot be claimed to guarantee transfer to squat, landing, sprint, cutting, or kicking tasks.

claims: Half-kneeling provides visible front-foot, heel, forward-knee, and rear-knee checkpoints.
Athlete support must also explain the uncounted first advance, small retreat, re-advance count, rear-knee comfort, permitted smaller range, unexpected symptoms, safe side change, and how to stop.

evidence.sourceTitle: Reliability and validity of a weight-bearing measure of ankle dorsiflexion range of motion
claims: Repeatable weight-bearing dorsiflexion measurement depends on standardized setup and contact observation.

Coach support must observe pad, rear-knee support, front heel and tripod, knee path, endpoints, range, foot rotation, trunk, breathing, first fault, actual exposure, symptoms, and downstream demands without diagnosing restriction.

evidence.sourceTitle: Immediate and Short Term Effect of Dry Needling on Triceps Surae Range of Motion and Functional Movement: A Randomized Trial
evidence.sourcePublisher: International Journal of Sports Physical Therapy
claims: The half-kneeling position can be demonstrated through visible support and heel-contact landmarks.

A thicker pad, smaller comfortable endpoint, shorter retreat, slower tempo, fewer pulses, more rest, visual marks, still images, captions, or live instruction can preserve the task; standing, elevated, wall-loaded, or clinician-assisted support requires separate review.

claims: The trial distinguishes banded step-supported mobilization, kettlebell-loaded kneeling dorsiflexion, and seated band-pull tasks.
Standing rockers, full-return kneeling rockers, banded, loaded, elevated, isometric, active-lift, calf-strength, calf-pulse, ankle-CAR, and clinical-test tasks remain distinct alternatives.

alternateAssessments.name: Half-Kneeling Ankle Dorsiflexion Pulse
alternateAssessments.rationale: Source 41's name matches the rear-knee-supported, planted-front-foot end-range pulse contract.

alternateAssessments.name: Half-Kneeling End-Range Ankle Pulse
alternateAssessments.rationale: This alias preserves support, contacts, partial retreat, re-advance, and count.

alternateAssessments.name: Comfortable Forward Endpoint
alternateAssessments.rationale: A smaller symptom-free endpoint changes amplitude without changing support, pulse action, or count.

alternateAssessments.name: Declared Partial-Retreat Distance
alternateAssessments.rationale: A small retreat distance is a pulse parameter while the knee remains near end range and returns to the same endpoint.

alternateAssessments.name: Front-Foot Placement
alternateAssessments.rationale: Declared foot placement is a setup parameter when contacts and the pulse contract remain fixed.

alternateAssessments.name: Light Fingertips on Front Thigh
alternateAssessments.rationale: Light non-unloading contact may support orientation while preserving front-foot and rear-knee loading.

alternateAssessments.name: Mat Thickness or Rear-Knee Padding
alternateAssessments.rationale: Approved padding changes comfort but not the rear-knee support identity.

alternateAssessments.name: Controlled Tempo or Brief Endpoint Pause
alternateAssessments.rationale: Pace and a brief pause change exposure time while preserving the pulse sequence.

alternateAssessments.name: Pulse Count Sets Rest or Side Order
alternateAssessments.rationale: Volume, recovery, and side sequence change delivery rather than identity.

alternateAssessments.name: Visual Knee Target or Breathing Prompt
alternateAssessments.rationale: Non-contact visual and breathing prompts clarify execution without adding an action.

alternateAssessments.name: Half-Kneeling Full-Return Ankle Rocker
alternateAssessments.rationale: Returning to the upright half-kneeling start changes the endpoint and repetition count.

alternateAssessments.name: Wall-Supported Half-Kneeling Ankle Pulse
alternateAssessments.rationale: Meaningful hand loading on a wall changes support, load distribution, station needs, and balance demand.

alternateAssessments.name: Band-Assisted Half-Kneeling Talocrural Mobilization
alternateAssessments.rationale: External band force changes equipment, anchor safety, force direction, setup, and clinical scope.

alternateAssessments.name: Kettlebell-Loaded Half-Kneeling Dorsiflexion
alternateAssessments.rationale: A kettlebell on the front knee changes load, physical difficulty, balance, failure consequences, and supervision.

alternateAssessments.name: Elevated-Front-Foot Half-Kneeling Mobilization
alternateAssessments.rationale: A step or box changes support geometry, equipment, range interpretation, and fall exposure.

alternateAssessments.name: Half-Kneeling Dorsiflexion with End-Range Activation
alternateAssessments.rationale: Actively lifting the forefoot at end range adds dorsiflexor contraction and a timed activation action.

alternateAssessments.name: Clinician-Assisted Half-Kneeling Mobilization
alternateAssessments.rationale: Manual force, clinical interpretation, consent, provider scope, and documentation change the task and service.

alternateAssessments.name: Standing Knee-to-Wall Ankle Rocker
alternateAssessments.rationale: Source 40 uses staggered standing bilateral-foot support and a complete forward-and-return cycle.

alternateAssessments.name: Wall Ankle Dorsiflexion Iso Press
alternateAssessments.rationale: Source 844 sustains an isometric press rather than repeating a small dynamic pulse.

alternateAssessments.name: Ankle CARs
alternateAssessments.rationale: Source 42 uses controlled ankle circumduction rather than weight-bearing sagittal pulsing.

alternateAssessments.name: Wall Lean Calf-Soleus Pulse
alternateAssessments.rationale: Source 1364 uses standing wall-lean support and a plantarflexor lower-leg pulse rather than rear-knee-supported dorsiflexion.

alternateAssessments.name: Calf Raise to Controlled Heel Drop
alternateAssessments.rationale: Source 44 lifts and lowers the heel through plantarflexion and eccentric return.

alternateAssessments.name: Clinical Half-Kneeling Dorsiflexion Test
alternateAssessments.rationale: A standardized maximal measurement adds interpretation, comparison, documentation, consent, and clinical scope.

alternateAssessments.name: Static Bent-Knee Calf or Soleus Stretch
alternateAssessments.rationale: A sustained stretch has a hold duration and tissue-bias contract rather than repeated retreat-and-re-advance pulses.
